## Intent
Hypothesis: delegating the Halide-expressible integration loop to AOT-compiled math can recover SIMD vectorization and approach the streaming ceiling, even with a simple scalar respawn loop.

## Layout & approach
The 68 B/p AoS Particle layout offers 11-field density but each loop touches only a sliver: loop 1 reads pos+vel = 24 of 68 B (35% hot), loop 2 reads age+seed = 8 of 68 B (11% hot), loop 3 reads color+pos = 28 of 68 B (41% hot). The remaining 59–89% per loop is dead weight dragged through the 128 B line filler. No intermediate storage is used — the death verdict stays in registers, avoiding a second pass but forcing loop 2 to carry the full 68 B stride. The approach delegates loop 1 to an external AOT Halide call (`_halide_b5_math`) and keeps loop 2 as a simple per-particle scan with select-based respawn. With 68 B/p, L1d spills at N≈963 and L2 at N≈61680; beyond those transitions the dead-byte fraction makes every DRAM fetch 3–9× over-provisioned.

## Cache saturation
The ns/p curve is strikingly flat across all N at every death rate. At q=0.01, cost holds at 8.0–8.7 ns/p from N=380 (L1d) through N=10M (DRAM) with no knee at the L1d spill (N≈963) or the L2 spill (N≈61680). At q=0.5 it holds at 13.5–14.2 ns/p equally flatly. This means the algo is never bandwidth-sensitive: if cache residency mattered, the DRAM regime would rise toward the 2.274 ns/p floor, but it does not. The dense grid resolves no spill because per-particle overhead — not line-fill latency — dominates every regime.

## Bandwidth
Achieved bandwidth peaks at 8.54 GB/s (q=0.01, N=100000) — 28% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling and 3.5× above the 2.274 ns/p memory floor. The algo is overhead-bound at low q (compute 62–68%, backend 27–31%) and transitions to branch-bound by q=0.25 (branch_flush 27–35%, backend dropping to 6–17%). Against baseline the margin is thin: 1.08–1.17× at q=0.01, collapsing to 1.00–1.07× at q=0.5 — at N=41000/q=0.25 it dips to 0.999×. Against the winner the algo is 1.74–2.33× slower at q=0.01 and 2.50–2.63× slower at q=0.5.

## Assembly
Zero vector instructions across all 345 insns — the `_halide_b5_math` AOT call (`bl 0x100052adc`) sets up eight stack buffer descriptors but produces no `q`/`v` register usage in the step body. Loop 2 is the cost center: 147 insns/iter, 15 conditional branches, 18 `csel` select-based respawn decisions, and 16 `strb` byte-granular scatter stores. The `ldrb` (×12) / `strb` (×16) pattern confirms byte-level color-channel access. Scalar FP (`fmul s5`, `fadd s5`, `fsub s5`) processes one particle per iteration. The `fcmp` (×9) / `csel` (×18) clamping chains explain the high instruction count. Stride-68B loads (`ldr s0, [x27], #0x44`) drag the full AoS struct for 8 hot bytes. Without SIMD, the 68 B/p fetch cannot be amortized across lanes, directly explaining the 28% ceiling utilization.

## Verdict
Refuted — the Halide AOT delegation produced zero vectorization (0/345 vector insns), yielding only 1.08–1.17× over naive at q=0.01 (8.0 ns/p vs the winner's ~3.5 ns/p, 1.74–2.33× slower) and collapsing to 1.00–1.07× at q=0.5 (2.50–2.63× slower) as branch_flush rises to 34–35%. The scalar `strb` scatter and `csel` respawn chain cannot stream, and the 65–89% dead-byte fraction in the 68 B/p AoS layout caps achieved BW at 28% of ceiling even at the best point.
